[[List of cities and towns in Rajasthan|third-largest]] city of the western [[Indian state]] of [[Rajasthan]].{{cite web |url=http://www.indiatravelportal.com/rajasthan-tourism/major-cities/ |title=Major Cities in Rajasthan |publisher=Indiatravelportal.com |access-date=2013-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130803094437/http://www.indiatravelportal.com/rajasthan-tourism/major-cities |archive-date=3 August 2013 |url-status=live}} It is located about 230 km (143 mi) south of the state capital, [[Jaipur]], on the banks of the [[Chambal River]]. As of 2024, with a population of over 1.5 million, it is the third most populous city in Rajasthan, after Jaipur and [[Jodhpur]].{{Cite web |title=Kota, India Metro Area Population 1950-2024 |url=https://www.macrotrends.net/global-metrics/cities/21310/kota/population#:~:text=The%20current%20metro%20area%20population,a%203%25%20increase%20from%202021. |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=www.macrotrends.net}} It is also India's first and world's second traffic signal free city after Bhutan's capital Thimphu. It serves as the administrative headquarters for the [[Kota district]] and [[Kota division]]. It was founded as a walled city in the 14th century in the erstwhile [[Bundi State|Bundi state]] and became the capital of the [[Kota state|princely state of Kota]] in 1625, following the separation of the Bundi and the Kota state.{{Cite web |title=Welcome to -Nagar Nigam Kota North |url=http://kotamc.org/UI/Static/Kotahistory.aspx#:~:text=The%20city%20of%20Kota%20(previously,the%20land%20of%20the%20Hadas. |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=kotamc.org}}{{Cite web |title=History of Kota, Bundi, Jhalawar : Books Collection |url=https://rgbooks.net/category/kota-bundi-jhalawar/#:~:text=RG%20Kota,%20Bundi,%20Jhala...&text=Kota,%20also%20spelled%20Kotah,%20city,%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A5%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A8%20%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%BE%20%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%BE%20%E0%A4%AC%E0%A4%A8%20%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A5%A4&text=Sale! |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=Rajasthani Granthagar |language=en-US}} Kota is renowned for its coaching institutes for [[engineering]] and [[medical]] entrance exams, such as [[Joint Entrance Examination|JEE]] and [[National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate)|NEET]]. Each year, over 200,000 students move to Kota to prepare for these competitive exams.{{Cite news |date=25 February 2025 |title=Kota administration announces new rules for hostels {{!}} Check details. |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/rajasthan/kota-administration-announces-new-rules-for-hostels-security-fee-waiver-installation-of-anti-suicide-ceiling-fans-latest-updates-2025-02-25-977932 |access-date=25 February 2025 |work=INDIA TV}} In addition to several monuments, Kota is known for its palaces and gardens.{{cite web|url=http://www.tsiindia.com/tours-to-rajasthan/tours-to-kota/|title=Tours to Kota|work=Indian Horizons|access-date=2016-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817130730/http://www.tsiindia.com/tours-to-rajasthan/tours-to-kota/|archive-date=17 August 2016|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=http://www.tsiindia.com/tours-to-rajasthan/tours-to-kota/lakes-and-gardens-in-kota-rajasthan.html|title=Lakes and Gardens in Kota|work=Indian Horizons|access-date=2016-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817143936/http://www.tsiindia.com/tours-to-rajasthan/tours-to-kota/lakes-and-gardens-in-kota-rajasthan.html|archive-date=17 August 2016|url-status=live}} The city was included among 98 Indian cities for the [[Smart Cities Mission]] initiated by the [[Prime Minister of India|Indian Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] in 2015{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/centre-releases-list-of-98-cities-for-smart-city-project/article7586751.ece|title=Centre unveils list of 98 smart cities; UP, TN strike it rich|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|access-date=2016-05-24|date=2015-08-28|author=Mehboob Jeelani|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161126124324/http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/centre-releases-list-of-98-cities-for-smart-city-project/article7586751.ece|archive-date=26 November 2016|url-status=live}} and was listed at 67th place after the results of the first round were released. Afterward, the top 20 cities were further selected for funding in the immediate financial year.{{cite web|url=http://smartcities.gov.in/writereaddata/Ranking_of_Smart%20Cities.pdf|title=Ranking of Smart Cities|publisher=Ministry of Urban Development|access-date=2016-05-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322215128/http://smartcities.gov.in/writereaddata/Ranking_of_Smart%20Cities.pdf|archive-date=22 March 2016|url-status=live}} ==History== {{see also|Kota State}} [[File:Mughal203.jpg|thumb|left|Procession of Raja Ram Singh II of Kota, Later Mughal Period, c. 1850]] [[File:Chambal river front view.jpg|thumb|left|Chambal riverfront]] [[File:Raja_Kotia_Bhil.jpg|thumb|left|Statue of King Kotia Bhil Smarak]] The history of the city dates back to the 12th century CE, when Rao Deva, a [[Chauhan Dynasty|Chauhan]] Rajput chieftain belonging to the [[Hada (clan)|Hada]] clan, conquered the territory and founded [[Bundi]] and [[Hadoti]]. Later, in the early 17th century, during the reign of the Mughal Emperor [[Jahangir]], the ruler of Bundi – Rao Ratan Singh, gave the smaller principality of Kota to his son, Madho Singh. Since then Kota has been recognized as a hallmark of the Rajput gallantry and culture. {| class="toccolours" border="1" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="2" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1em; width: 250px; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 95%;" |- | colspan="2" style="margin-left:inherit; background:pink; text-align:center; font-size:medium;"|Princely city: '''Kota (कोटा)''' |- style="vertical-align: top;" | '''Region''' | [[Hadoti]] |- style="vertical-align: top;" | '''19th-century [[flag]]''' | [[File:Flag of Kotah.svg|50px]] |- style="vertical-align: top;" | '''Independence from:''' | [[Bundi State]] |- style="vertical-align: top;" | '''State existed:''' | 1579–1949 |- style="vertical-align: top;" | '''[[Dynasty|Dynasties]]''' | Rajput Chauhan Hada |- style="vertical-align: top;" | '''[[Capital (political)|Capital]]''' | Kota |- style="vertical-align: top;" | |} [[File:Indian - Dewali celebrations at Kotah - Google Art Project.jpg|thumb|left|[[Diwali]] celebrations at Kota, 1690s]] Kota became an independent state in 1631 when Rao Madho Singh, the second son of Rao Ratan of [Bundi], was made the ruler by the Mughal Emperor [[Jahangir]]. Soon, Kota outgrew its parent state as it expanded in area, became wealthier in revenue, and more powerful. Maharao Bhim Singh played a pivotal role in Kota's history, having held a 'Mansab'{{cite web|url=http://www.mapsofindia.com/kota/history.html|title=History of Kota|work=Maps of India|access-date=5 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808092932/http://www.mapsofindia.com/kota/history.html|archive-date=8 August 2016|url-status=live}} of five thousand and being the first in his dynasty to have the title of [[Maharao]]. Zalim Singh, a diplomat and statesman, emerged as another prominent figure of the state in the 18th century. Although initially being a general of Kota's army, he rose to the regent of the kingdom after the king died, leaving a minor on the throne.{{cite web|url=http://www.rajasthantravel.org.uk/kota/|title=About Kota|work=Rajasthan Travel Guide & News |publisher=Rajasthan Travel|access-date=2016-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160908203327/http://www.rajasthantravel.org.uk/kota/|archive-date=8 September 2016|url-status=live}} He remained a direct administrator of the state. In 1817, a treaty of friendship was signed between him and the British on the condition of carving out part of the existing state for his descendants, resulting in the formation of [[Jhalawar State]] in 1838. Kota was not involved in the earlier events of the [[Indian Rebellion of 1857]]. However, when in October 1857, rebels murdered the local British resident and his two sons, British forces responded by storming the city and, after some resistance, capturing it in March 1858.{{cite book|last=Llewellyn-Jones|first=Rosie|title=The Great Uprising in India, Untold Stories. ''Chapter Two: The Kotah Residency Murders''.|pages=66–95|publisher=Boydell & Brewer, England|year=2007|isbn=978-1843833048}} In the 1940s, social activist [[Guru Radha Kishan]] organised trade union activities and campaigned against the colonial government. He left Kota after the local administration learned of the arrest warrant issued against him for his participation in Indian Independence activities. ==Geography== [[File:Kishore-Sagar-Lake-Kota.jpeg|Kishore Sagar Lake|thumb|left]] Kota is situated along the banks of the [[Chambal River]] in the southern part of [[Rajasthan]]. It is the third-largest [[city]] of Rajasthan after [[Jaipur]] and [[Jodhpur]]. The cartographic coordinates are {{Coord|25.18|N|75.83|E|}}.{{Cite web |url=http://www.fallingrain.com/world/IN/24/Kota.html |title=Falling Rain Genomics, Inc – Kota |access-date=2 November 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070311222250/http://www.fallingrain.com/world/IN/24/Kota.html |archive-date=11 March 2007 |url-status=live}} It covers an area of {{Convert|221.36|km2|abbr=on}}.{{Cite web|url=http://kotamc.org/UI/Static/cityprofile.aspx|title=City Profile|website=kotamc.org|access-date=21 November 2020|archive-date=25 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425014846/http://kotamc.org/UI/Static/cityprofile.aspx|url-status=dead}}[http://www.rajasthan.gov.in/KOTA1.SHTM Statistics by Govt. of Rajasthan] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070629033725/http://www.rajasthan.gov.in/KOTA1.SHTM |date=29 June 2007 }} It has an average elevation of 271 metres (889 ft). The district is bound on the north and northwest by [[Sawai Madhopur]], [[Tonk district|Tonk]], and [[Bundi]] districts. The Chambal River separates these districts from the Kota district, forming the natural boundary. The city of Kota is situated at the centre of the southeastern region of Rajasthan, a region very widely known as [[Hadoti]], the land of the [[Hada (clan)|Hadas]]. Kota lies along the banks of the Chambal river on a high sloping tableland forming a part of the Malwa Plateau. The general slope of the city is towards the north. The comparatively rocky, barren, and elevated land in the southern part of the city descends towards a plain agricultural land in the north. The Mukundara hills run from the southeast to the northwest axis of the town. Kota has fertile land and greenery with irrigation facilities through canals. The two main canals, referred to as the left main canal (towards Bundi) and the right main canal (towards Baran), originate from the reservoir created by [[Kota Barrage]].{{cite web|url=http://kotadivision.nic.in/commandareadevlopment.htm|title=COMMAND AREA DEVELOPMENT CHAMBAL, KOTA|access-date=3 July 2016|publisher=kotadivision.nic.in|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323190452/http://kotadivision.nic.in/commandareadevlopment.htm|archive-date=23 March 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://waterresources.rajasthan.gov.in/4chambal.htm |title=Chambal Valley Project |publisher=Water Resources Department, Govt. of Rajasthan |access-date=3 July 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304085442/http://waterresources.rajasthan.gov.in/4chambal.htm |archive-date= 4 March 2016 }} The tributaries of these canals form a network in the city and surrounding areas of Rajasthan and [[Madhya Pradesh]], and supplements the irrigation of these areas. ===Climate=== {{climate chart |Kota |10.6|23.2|10 |12.8|26.0|20 |18.6|32.7|10 |24.8|38.6|10 |29.3|42.1|20 |28.5|39.6|50 |26.2|33.6|250 |25.9|31.5|240 |25.0|34.3|110 |22.0|34|20 |15.6|29.6|10 |12.0|25.1|10 |source=[http://www.mustseeindia.com/Kota-weather Kota weather] |float=right |clear=none }} Kota has a semi-arid climate ([[Köppen climate classification]] ''BSh''), bordering on a [[Monsoon-influenced humid subtropical climate]] (Köppen: Cwa), with high temperatures throughout the year. Summers are long, hot, and dry, starting in late March and lasting till the end of June. The temperatures average above 40 °C in May and June, frequently exceed 45 °C, with temperatures as high as 48.5 °C have also been recorded.{{cite web|url=http://zeenews.india.com/news/nation/heat-wave-claims-10-lives-kota-hottest-at-484-c_629219.html|title=Heat wave claims 10 lives; Kota hottest at 48.4 °C|date=26 May 2010|access-date=23 April 2016|publisher=Zee News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160921131042/http://zeenews.india.com/news/nation/heat-wave-claims-10-lives-kota-hottest-at-484-c_629219.html|archive-date=21 September 2016|url-status=live}} The monsoon season follows with comparatively lower temperatures, but higher humidity and frequent, torrential downpours. The monsoons subside in October and temperatures rise again. The brief, mild winter starts in late November and lasts until the last week of February. Temperatures hover between 26.7 °C (max) to 12.0 °C (min). This can be considered the best time to visit Kota because of the intense heat in the summer.{{cite web|url=https://weather-and-climate.com/average-monthly-Rainfall-Temperature-Sunshine,Kota,India|title=Kota Climate details: Monthly Temperature, Rainfall and Sunshine|access-date=2016-05-08|publisher=Weather and climate.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605055402/https://weather-and-climate.com/average-monthly-Rainfall-Temperature-Sunshine,Kota,India|archive-date=5 June 2016|url-status=live}} The average annual rainfall in the [[Kota district]] is 800.6 mm. Most of the rainfall can be attributed to the southwest [[monsoon]], which usually begins around the last week of June and may last till mid-September. Pre-monsoon showers usually occur around the middle of June, with post-monsoon rains occasionally occurring in October. Over the last 15 years, Kota has emerged as an Education hub of the country as producing excellent results in [[IIT-JEE]] and medical entrance exams.{{cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/education/jee-main-2016-results-kota-institutes-excel-again/story-ma4PKJT9lTebAAOHBx9rWO.html|title=JEE (Main) 2016 results: Kota institutes excel again|newspaper=[[Hindustan Times]]|access-date=4 June 2016|date=29 April 2016|author=Aabshar H Quazi|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531212655/http://www.hindustantimes.com/education/jee-main-2016-results-kota-institutes-excel-again/story-ma4PKJT9lTebAAOHBx9rWO.html|archive-date=31 May 2016|url-status=live}}{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Top-3-in-IIT-entrance-exam-from-Kota-institute/articleshow/52720569.cms|title=Top 3 in IIT entrance exam from Kota institute|newspaper=[[The Times of India]]|access-date=2 July 2016|date=13 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616041854/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Top-3-in-IIT-entrance-exam-from-Kota-institute/articleshow/52720569.cms|archive-date=16 June 2016|url-status=live}} === Kota educational industry === Kota is recognised as a major center for competitive [[test preparation]], attracting around 150,000 students each year, as reported in 2023. These students come from across the country to enroll in coaching institutes that prepare them for national entrance exams for engineering and medical colleges. The industry generates an estimated $350–$450 million annually, with over 300 coaching centers, including the Allen Career Institute, which tutors more than one million students nationwide.{{Cite web |last=Choksi |first=Mansi |date=January 18, 2023 |title=Inside India's Cram City |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/18/magazine/india-cram-schools-kota.html |website=[[The New York Times Magazine]]}} The coaching industry in Kota originated in the 1980s when [[Vinod Kumar Bansal]], a mechanical engineer, began tutoring students after being diagnosed with a degenerative condition that confined him to a wheelchair. His methods, inspired by the [[Kumon]] method of learning, emphasized systematic problem solving. Bansal's success in helping students gain admission to prestigious institutions like the [[Indian Institutes of Technology]] (IIT) drew more students to the city. Over time, other coaching centers were established by former colleagues and associates, eventually transforming Kota into an educational hub. ===Kota Doria or Kota Doriya and Sarees=== {{Main|Kota doria}} [[File:Kota sari with gota patti by ashish 01.JPG|thumb|right|Kota Sari with [[Gota Patti]] embroidery]] Weaving in Kota was started by Maharana Bhimdev in the 18th century.{{cite news |url=http://www.hindu.com/mp/2005/04/02/stories/2005040202100100.htm |title=Metro Plus Delhi / Arts & Crafts : Let's go Kota |date=2005-04-02 |access-date=2013-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318105910/http://www.hindu.com/mp/2005/04/02/stories/2005040202100100.htm |archive-date=18 March 2014 |newspaper=[[The Hindu]] |url-status=dead}} The Kota saris, like most traditional pieces of work, had started becoming lost before designer Vidhi Singhania moved to Kota and started working with the workers to revive its market.{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/thehindu/mp/2003/03/12/stories/2003031200400100.htm|title=A piece of 'tradition'|access-date=2016-04-20|date=2003-03-12|author=Radhika Rajamani|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040117204920/http://www.thehindu.com/thehindu/mp/2003/03/12/stories/2003031200400100.htm|archive-date=17 January 2004|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|url-status=dead}} Many textile shops in the city sell different varieties of Kota doriya. These saris have become one of the trademarks of the city. {{cite web|url=http://www.kotaheritagesociety.in/khs/kota-doria/articles/kota-doria.html|title=Kota doriya – unique summer weave|publisher=Kota Heritage Society|access-date=2016-04-20|author=Ritu Jain and Victoria Singh|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160814043505/http://www.kotaheritagesociety.in/khs/kota-doria/articles/kota-doria.html|archive-date=14 August 2016|url-status=live}} ===Kota stone=== [[File:Aire de stockage de pierre de Kota.jpg|thumb|right|Storage area of Kota Stone]] {{Main|Kota Stone}} The fine-grained variety of limestone quarried from the Kota district is known as Kota stone, with rich greenish-blue and brown colours. Kota stone is tough, non-water-absorbent, non-slip, and non-porous. The varieties include Kota Blue Natural, Kota Blue Honed, Kota Blue Polished, Kota Blue Cobbles, Kota Brown Natural, and Kota Brown Polished.{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/features/homes-and-gardens/kota-for-a-fresh-look/article3750325.ece|title=Kota, for a fresh look|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|author=Sathya Prakash Varanashi|access-date=20 May 2016|date=20 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911135258/http://www.thehindu.com/features/homes-and-gardens/kota-for-a-fresh-look/article3750325.ece|archive-date=11 September 2017|url-status=live}} ===Food=== Kota is famous for Dal Kachori. ===Industries=== Kota is one of the industrial hubs in [[northern India]], with chemical, cement, engineering, and power plants based there. Kota ( ), previously known as Kotah, is the third-largest city of the western Indian state of Rajasthan. It is located about 230 km (143 mi) south of the state capital, Jaipur, on the banks of the Chambal River. As of 2024, with a population of over 1.5 million, it is the third most populous city in Rajasthan, after Jaipur and Jodhpur. It is also India's first and world's second traffic signal free city after Bhutan's capital Thimphu. It serves as the administrative headquarters for the Kota district and Kota division. It was founded as a walled city in the 14th century in the erstwhile Bundi state and became the capital of the princely state of Kota in 1625, following the separation of the Bundi and the Kota state. Kota is renowned for its coaching institutes for engineering and medical entrance exams, such as JEE and NEET. Each year, over 200,000 students move to Kota to prepare for these competitive exams.
In addition to several monuments, Kota is known for its palaces and gardens. The city was included among 98 Indian cities for the Smart Cities Mission initiated by the Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015 and was listed at 67th place after the results of the first round were released. Afterward, the top 20 cities were further selected for funding in the immediate financial year.
